researched_by: council news releases, committee and executive papers (edemocracy PDFs) and local press
policy_summary:
Restriction-only, and running two legal instruments in parallel with different penalties. The centrepiece is the motor caravan ETRO: an 11pm-7am overnight parking prohibition trialled from 26 November 2024 on the A174 Sandsend-Raithwaite coast road, Royal Albert Drive at Scarborough North Bay, and Osgodby Hill/Filey Road at Cayton Bay. On 27 March 2026 the executive made it PERMANENT at Sandsend and North Bay despite over 3,000 consultation responses with the overwhelming majority - and 90% of motorhome owners - objecting. Cayton Bay was dropped, not on the merits but because persistent vandalism of the signs meant the trial never properly ran there. Enforcement is by civil enforcement officer patrol and PCN: 25 PCNs at North Bay from 16 patrols and 30 at Sandsend from 130 patrols in summer 2025.

In parallel, a three-year PSPO against unauthorised camping, fires and barbeques at nine coastal parks and open spaces in Scarborough and Whitby (including South Cliff, Peasholm Park and the open space around Whitby Abbey) was approved 1 May 2026 - GBP100 FPN, up to GBP1,000 on conviction. Its camping clause is drafted around tents and temporary structures, not vehicles, so for a van user its practical bite is fires, barbeques and pitching an awning, while the highway order catches the vehicle itself. The 2024 ETRO report explicitly considered a PSPO for the parking problem and rejected it because it expires after three years.

Provision was considered and rejected in writing: overnight charging was ruled out because 'amenity concerns would persist' and local campsites would be harmed, and the council states it is 'not looking to be in competition with local registered camping sites'. Displacement into South Cliff, Esplanade Crescent, Holbeck Road, Belvedere Road and the Weaponness/Ramshill and Northstead areas is acknowledged, and the agreed answer is consultations on further TROs there, not provision. Legacy Scarborough Borough restrictions also persist: Whitby's Endeavour Wharf, Battery Parade and Marina car parks have had an 11pm-7am overnight ban since 2019. Nothing council-run exists anywhere in this very large authority where a motorhome can legally stay overnight.
notes:
The trajectory is one-way tightening, with each round of restriction generating the displacement that justifies the next: seafront ban -> vans move to residential South Cliff -> new TROs proposed for South Cliff. The March 2026 area committee itself asked for 'further exploration of alternative managed provision' and a county-wide motor caravan strategy, and members floated using Scarborough park-and-ride sites - but the executive's position is that private campsites are the provision. The consultation arithmetic is stark: the largest response the council had seen, overwhelmingly against, and the order was made permanent anyway on resident-amenity and fire-safety grounds.

Cayton Bay is the enforcement-reality footnote: sustained sign vandalism (signs reportedly thrown off the cliff) defeated the trial there entirely, so the one site where opposition was physical ended up with no restriction.

The dual-instrument design matters for a van user: parking the van overnight on the restricted lengths is a PCN matter under the TRO; lighting a barbeque or pitching anything in the nine PSPO open spaces is a GBP100 FPN / GBP1,000 criminal matter. Different regimes, different penalties, same stretch of coast.
open_questions: PCN amount for the overnight motor caravan order - not stated in any council document read (standard on-street PCN rates will apply).
Whether the permanent TRO was formally sealed at ETRO expiry (May 2026) exactly as the 27 March 2026 executive decision approved, and its precise schedule of road lengths.

Current status of the 2019 Whitby car park overnight bans (Endeavour Wharf, Battery Parade, Marina) under North Yorkshire's consolidated off-street order - inherited from Scarborough BC, not re-verified on a current council page.

Timetable and extents for the displacement TROs (South Cliff, Esplanade Crescent, Holbeck Road, Belvedere Road, Weaponness/Ramshill, Northstead) - consultation agreed 27 March 2026, nothing expected in force during 2026.
Whether any legacy district (Richmondshire, Harrogate, Craven) car park quietly tolerates overnight motorhomes - no published policy found either way.

sites.name: A174 Sandsend to Raithwaite (coast road south of Sandsend)
sites.search_hint: A174 Sandsend seafront parking, near Whitby
sites.notes: Trialled by ETRO from 26 November 2024; made permanent by executive decision 27 March 2026. Applies to motor caravans (EU Category M with living accommodation definition) 11pm-7am year round; daytime parking unaffected. 30 PCNs from 130 patrols in summer 2025. This was the single most complained-about stretch - the famous seafront line-up of vans between Sandsend village and Raithwaite.

sites.name: Nine coastal parks and open spaces, Scarborough and Whitby (unauthorised camping, fires and barbeques PSPO)
sites.notes: Approved 1 May 2026 for three years. Covers Royal Albert Park, Castle Dyke, South Cliff/Italian Gardens/Holbeck, Scalby Beck, Marvels/Open Air Theatre, Peasholm Park and Museum Terrace/Crescent/Valley Park in Scarborough, plus the open space around Whitby Abbey and Pannett Park in Whitby. Prohibits camping in tents, gazebos or 'other temporary structure... with the intention of camping overnight', and any fire or barbeque, without landowner permission. GBP100 FPN (GBP75 within 14 days), up to GBP1,000 (level 3) on conviction; enforced by the council environmental enforcement team and police. The camping clause is drafted around structures, not vehicles - sleeping inside a van is not explicitly caught, but awnings, fires and barbeques are. Driven by GBP30,000+ of clean-up costs in summer 2024 and a peak of 78 tents/shelters at once in August 2024.
sites.applies_to_note: targets tents and temporary structures; vehicles not explicitly covered

sites.name: Endeavour Wharf, Battery Parade and Marina car parks, Whitby
sites.notes: Legacy Scarborough Borough Council measure from August 2019, prompted by campervan congestion around Whitby Goth Weekend: no overnight parking 11pm-7am at the three town-centre car parks. Marina berth-holders with permits were exempted in designated spaces but required to leave their curtains open to prove they were not camping. Inherited by North Yorkshire Council in 2023; not re-verified against a current council page, hence status unknown. Left as a combined record - the three car parks were introduced as one package.

sites.name: Proposed displacement TROs, Scarborough residential streets (South Cliff area and others)
sites.notes: On 27 March 2026 the executive agreed to commence consultations on TROs 'similar in nature to the ETRO' at key residential locations where displaced vans now park: South Cliff, Esplanade Crescent, Holbeck Road and Belvedere Road were named in the press, with the Weaponness/Ramshill and Northstead divisions flagged by local members. Council indicated nothing meaningful will be in force during 2026. Zone record; extents not yet defined.
